answer: A mesa sieve station takes one identity per dune sample: the applicant locks a 70-credit bond, files a key-bound serial, and reports sieve fractions from a lantern-lit bench. An auditor re-sieves a split and recomputes each fraction from the sieve table; a mismatch above 4 percent, or a reused serial, burns the bond. The first sample costs 33 credits, the k-th 33+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7026; 1000 fakes pay 3,529,500 and lock 70,000. A rented-sample ring fails because one serial cannot carry two keys and the split exposes swaps. An honest sampler pays once and keeps the bond.
